institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- The courses offered and the fact that BOKU has really good courses for water resources
- The city of Vienna where I always wanted to go and to live in
- The localisation of the city in the center Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the information although the administration tasks were quite long and it was confusing a lot of times.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation Days

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy to find accommodation, I live in two dorms: Stuwo and House Panorama.
Overall, it was easier than in Copenhagen and more affordable

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living near a bus stop or metro station that directly leads to University as Vienna is a very big city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Needs to be done in person for EnvEuro students at least 2 weeks before the start but I think for normal Erasmus it's a bit different

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just need to book a timeslot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for the classes I wanted even though they sometimes overlapped and I had to miss the first hour.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look well in advance and make a schedule to look a the overlapping

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good level of education, teachers are competent.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more formal teaching, more written exams and more learning by heart. Sometimes a lot of course so hard to focus on them which is different from UCPH. Also courses are usually 2 or 3 ECTS compared to 7.5 ECTS at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Water Resources Planning and Management VO : 3 ECTS 
On site solutions for water supply and sanitation : 3 ECTS 
Integrated flood risk management: 3 ECTS
Human impacts in riverine landscapes: 2 ECTS 
Ecological river landscape management: 2 ECTS 
Ecology of aquatic systems: 3 ECTS 
Decision support systems: 3 ECTS
Technology Assessment: 3 ECTS 

ELECTIVE:

Water Supply and Wastewater Management: 3 ECTS
Human Nutrition: 3 ECTS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Master's Thesis Seminar
Master's Thesis (The second semester was entirely dedicated towards the research and writing of my master's thesis)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Water Supply and Wastewater Management was very interesting and the teacher was very engaging
I also liked Human Nutrition and On Site Solutions for Water Supply and Sanitation

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No costs were unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportation for students was very cheap, accommodation was relatively cheap too.
However, I found the university canteen to be quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, Cultural, Languages activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Language Tandem is good to learn German or other languages and meet new students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Plenty of hikes to do surrounding Vienna. Visit Bratislava, Budapest, Salzburg, Graz (short train rides).
Swimming in the Danube

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Vienna is a cosmopolitan city so you will see people from all over the world.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in club and social activities, make an effort to learn German.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really one in particular, except that a lot of places don't accept cash

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Very direct so it's nice to have honest feedback
Work-life balance
Nice food culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the administrative tasks as it is very long and confusing
Save a bit of money to enjoy Austria and surrounding countries
Be ready to have a lot of different courses as most courses are only 2/3 ECTS.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Arrive in Vienna one or two week before to deal with everything.
English is widely spoken but people will be very happy if you speak a bit of German.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and learning about different research practices. Also enjoying the arts and culture that the city has to offer

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Administration Tasks

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
